task:
List tokens from marked.lexer do not describe what renders. The parser and renderer invent tokens and reshape them at render time. So a walkTokens hook or a custom renderer sees a different structure from the final HTML, and loose task lists render with a stray newline. All list structure must be final when the lexer returns. Task checkboxes become real tokens. For '- [ ] item 1\n- [x] item 2\n', each list_item keeps task: true, checked (false, then true), loose: false and text ('item 1', then 'item 2'), and its raw stays the same. Its tokens now start with a checkbox token ahead of the text token: { type: 'checkbox', raw: '[ ] ', checked: false } and { type: 'checkbox', raw: '[x] ', checked: true }. The Tokens.Checkbox type has type, raw and checked. A list item that is not a task must have no checked property at all, not even checked: undefined. In a loose list, block text tokens inside items become type 'paragraph', with raw, text and tokens unchanged. For '- item 1\n\n- item 2' the first token of each item has type 'paragraph'. For an item with two blocks, as in '- item 2\n\n item 2a\n', both are paragraphs, with the space token between them. In a loose task item, the checkbox token goes first inside the tokens of the item's first paragraph, and that paragraph's raw and text gain the checkbox raw as a prefix. If the item has no leading paragraph or text token, a new paragraph token holds just the checkbox. Rendering. renderer.checkbox receives the token and now writes its own trailing space: ' ', with checked="" ahead of disabled when checked. renderer.listitem just wraps the parsed tokens in
